title: Public Universe: explore space and prepare an observing night
summary: Unreleased review draft for the first Public Universe community release. The proposed batch combines easier astronomy discovery with private observing workspaces, explained night-planning windows and clearer scientific provenance. Features described here remain in development pull requests; this is not a launch announcement.

Explore and learn: Explore, Observe, Learn and Data offer starting points for children, teachers, observers and researchers. Public catalogue browsing and learning remain free without an account.

Search solar-system objects and exoplanets together, with results from an available catalogue retained if the other is unavailable. Live searches keep the browser title aligned with the current query.

Browse measured planetary systems with ordinary name and distance filters, then open their planets or locate them on the galaxy map. The optional 3D display loads only when requested; its loading guidance changes when it is ready.

Learning activities explain stellar distances, discovery methods and measurements. Meteor-shower pages retain distinct observation campaigns and approximate seasonal guidance, not visibility forecasts.

Native filters, pagination, clearer keyboard focus and mobile navigation improve access. Orrery dates and partial positions, close-approach limits and small uncertainties have clearer validation and explanations.
Keep your own observing workspace: Save named telescopes, binoculars, eyepieces, Barlows, reducers, cameras and observing sites in your browser. Known measurements retain explicit units; unknown values remain unknown.
Sites can include a user-entered horizon profile. Import files are previewed before replacement, older workspace files remain supported, and imported sites are not silently activated.

Create observing lists and record actual observation times, outcomes and notes. Equipment and site snapshots preserve historical context after later profile changes. A planned target or list status is not proof of an observation.
Download JSON, CSV or print views with explicit location choices. Keep exports private: notes, dates and derived context can still reveal personal information even when coordinates are omitted.

An optional account copy requires explicit preview and consent to upload, restore or remove it. Signing in does not transfer your local records. Conflicts require a fresh choice rather than silent overwrite.

Account copies are encrypted by the server, not end-to-end encrypted. Removing an account copy leaves guest-browser data separate; local storage replacement still requires care when editing in several tabs.
Prepare a night, with its limits explain: Choose a date, time zone, rounded location and available hours, or explicitly copy a saved site. The night calculation applies your minimum altitude, supplied horizon, darkness and Moon-separation choices.
Accessible charts and tables explain geometric windows for the Moon, planets and supported starter-catalogue targets. Empty, unresolved and unavailable results have distinct meanings.
Optional weather is requested separately for matching forecast hours. Missing or out-of-range forecasts stay unknown; clear weather does not establish that a target is observable.

Compare saved or temporary eyepieces by magnification, exit pupil and estimated field width, with field-stop values preferred when available. Camera previews use sensor geometry. These are geometric comparisons, not sky images or detection promises.

Forthcoming equipment comparisons add sourced magnitude bands, quality flags and angular-size context to a plan. Unknown dimensions and historical double-star separations do not become invented target diameters.

Forthcoming session downloads retain normalized inputs, windows, UTC times, time zone and method details. Coordinates and terrain are omitted by default and included only by explicit choice; CSV is a window index, while companion JSON carries fuller assumptions.

Seeing, sky brightness, optical quality, equipment compatibility and unmeasured obstacles can still prevent a useful view. This platform does not control telescopes or provide solar-observing instructions.
Read the source behind a result: A bounded starter catalogue brings sourced bright stars, overlapping historical multiple-star records and deep-sky objects into browsing and planning. It is not a complete sky survey; unsupported coordinates remain unavailable for calculation.
Coordinate frames, reference epochs, proper-motion assumptions and source-specific attribution remain visible. Unknown observation epochs or physical stellar distances are not filled with estimates.
Night calculations report their actual model, Earth-orientation data and, when configured, the checksum-pinned JPL kernel. Numerical boundary tolerance is not a statement of astronomical accuracy.
Catalogue metadata distinguishes a logical data identity from a build identity and downloadable-file checksums. Older, changed or unavailable catalogues can have unknown identity.

The frontend observes catalogue identity to separate cache generations and compares API metadata with downloadable database metadata. An identity observed in a separate request does not certify that every result belongs to an immutable snapshot.

Filtered exoplanet-page downloads retain original measurements, units, limits, uncertainties and references. Exact repetition still needs retained source snapshots, original inputs and compatible calculation software; a moving live API is not an archive.
Before this becomes a release: All changes in this draft are unreleased. Catalogue/session integration and equipment comparisons still need their combined acceptance checks before the final release scope is selected.
Local regression tests and selected browser checks do not establish field performance or physical-touch acceptance. Broader device, memory and map-render measurements remain programme work.
The existing public addresses remain in use. The move to publicuniverse.net, live backend prerequisites, deployment and community announcement are separate decisions.
The permanent release page will be published only after the selected running version is verified. This draft does not change the application version or publish any notes.
